title: Alias count is aggregated per level across sibling fragments; fragment-expanded selections count toward the total cap
answers: how are GraphQL aliases counted when split across fragments
why does MLFLOW_SERVER_GRAPHQL_MAX_ALIASES count sibling fragments together
GraphQL fragment cycle causes infinite loop in query scanner
body:
Invariant: All aliases at one selection-set level, including those from sibling inline fragments and spreads, are summed into one per-level count before comparing to the alias limit (scan_query takes max over levels). Splitting aliases across fragments must not lower the count.
Enforcement: mlflow/server/graphql/graphql_no_batching.py:_collect_fields_and_aliases returns total_aliases for the level; scan_query tracks max_aliases. Expanded fragment fields also increment total_selections and are checked against _MAX_SELECTIONS, so expansion cannot bypass the total cap.
Cycle guard: _collect_fields_and_aliases keeps a per-collection local_visited set seeded from the per-path visited_fragments frozenset; scan_query passes visited_fragments down the stack, and _MAX_DEPTH bounds recursion.
Do not: propagate local_visited into child levels. A fragment reused at two depths (for example at the root and inside a field) would be skipped deeper, undercounting fields and aliases and weakening the limit.
applies: Applies to changes to scan_query or _collect_fields_and_aliases in mlflow/server/graphql/graphql_no_batching.py.
says: Query scanner hangs indefinitely when processing requests containing circular query fragments
Requests bypass maximum alias limits by splitting alias fields across multiple fragments
Large queries evade field selection caps through nested fragment expansion
Enforce query complexity limits so sibling fragments cannot circumvent maximum alias quotas
Prevent infinite recursion and resource exhaustion during complex API query validation
search: In mlflow/server/graphql/graphql_no_batching.py, scan_query and _collect_fields_and_aliases aggregate all aliases at each selection-set level across sibling inline fragments and spreads against the alias limit. Expanded fragment fields increment total_selections checked against _MAX_SELECTIONS, with recursion bounded by _MAX_DEPTH and a visited_fragments frozenset path to prevent cycles. The local_visited set must not be propagated into child levels, which would skip reused fragments and undercount fields and aliases.
